title: Test catalog
intro: Keep a shared list of tests, decide which ones this lab offers, and link the codes received from your data sources. A catalog test and a result field are different things. One test can produce several result fields.
This setup is optional. OpenLDR can receive and process lab data before you configure it. We strongly recommend setting it up during use. The Lab order form offers the tests enabled at this lab.
Use your own test codes, names, specimens and files. The screenshots use fictional examples. No documentation sample data is required. Optional practice files are at the end.

Reading needs Browse terminology. Changes need Manage terminology. When the catalog comes from central, this lab can change local availability, specimens and names. It cannot change the shared test definitions.

The screenshots use an installation that owns its catalog. Result-field examples also use a small fictional result dictionary. Reference-band numbers are for documentation only. Use the ranges and code meanings approved for your actual tests.

tasks.title: Add a test to your catalog
intro: Use this for one new test when this installation owns its catalog. Search for an existing test before adding another code.
steps: Select Test catalog in the main menu on the left.
Select Tests, then open the dots beside its search and table controls.
Select Add test. The test sheet opens.
Enter the stable code from your own catalog. The fictional example uses EXAMPLE-ALPHA. Leave it empty only if the LOINC code should become the code. A saved code cannot be changed.
Enter the name people should see. A short name is optional. The example uses Example panel Alpha and Example Alpha.
Select the category that fits this test from the configured list. Categories come from Terminology.
Tick the specimen types this test accepts. Use the configured choices for your actual test.

tasks.title: Finish and save the test
intro: Continue in the open test sheet. You can configure this lab and result fields after saving the shared definition.
steps: Enter a confirmed LOINC code if you have one, or leave it blank. When LOINC is loaded, search and select a term. Here it is not loaded, so typed codes are checked for format only.
Select the dots in the test sheet, below its heading.
Select Save. New tests use Save too.
tasks.result: The sheet closes and the new test appears in Tests. It starts Off at this lab unless you enabled it in the sheet.

tasks.title: Make a test available at this lab
intro: Enable the tests this lab actually performs. This changes local availability, which the Lab order form uses.
steps: Select the dots at the right end of the test row.
Choose Switch on at this lab
Select Switch on at this lab. The same action becomes Switch off at this lab for an enabled test.
tasks.result: On at this lab reads On. Imported tests do not become enabled automatically.

tasks.title: Set this lab's name and specimen choices
intro: Use local settings when this lab uses a different display name or accepts fewer specimens. A lab receiving the catalog from central can still change these settings.
steps: Open the row dots menu and select Edit. The saved code is shown without an editable input.
Under This lab, use On at this lab to choose whether this lab offers the test.
Keep the specimen types this lab accepts. The local choices can narrow the catalog list. Keeping every specimen follows the catalog list.
Enter a local name if needed
Enter the local display name in the local-name field, or leave it blank to use the catalog name. The example uses Alpha at this lab.
Open the sheet dots menu and select Save.
tasks.result: The lab settings are saved without changing the test code.

tasks.title: Find and export tests
intro: Search before creating another test. You can also export active catalog tests for review or later import.
steps: Use Search code or name. Search also matches short and local names. The example finds the test using its local name.
Check the code and catalog name before editing. The test keeps its catalog name even when a local name matched your search.
Choose Export CSV when you need a file
Clear the search if you no longer need it. Open the Tests dots menu and select Export CSV to download active catalog tests. A central-managed lab can export too.
tasks.result: The browser downloads a CSV in the columns the import wizard understands. Export contains active catalog tests, not just a visible row.

tasks.title: Choose and map your test-list file
intro: Use an import when you have a list in CSV or Excel .xlsx format. Tests match by code. An import does not retire tests absent from the file or change local lab settings.
steps: On Tests, open the page dots menu and select Import.
Select the file area and choose your own CSV or XLSX file. The wizard reads it and opens Step 2 of 4: Columns.
Check every suggested column. Name is required. Correct a field using its selector beside the label.
Not in the file leaves an existing field unchanged. An empty cell in a selected column clears that field. Do not map an empty column unless that is intended.
Open the import sheet dots menu and select Next.

tasks.title: Resolve values and review the import
intro: The Values step lists category or specimen text that matched no configured choice. Decide what each text means before applying the file.
steps: Read the text and affected row count. A value left Not chosen causes its row to be refused. This example has an unrecognised category.
Select an existing category with the same meaning. Choose Add as a new category only when a new category is intended.
When adding a category, check or change its generated code. This example adds a fictional category. Resolve unmatched specimens through their choices too.
Open the sheet dots menu and select Next.
Check New, Changed, Unchanged and Refused, any refusal reasons, and Categories to add. Use Back in the dots menu if you need to correct the file decisions.
When the review matches your intention, open the sheet dots menu and select Apply. Nothing is written before this action.
tasks.result: The sheet closes and imported tests appear. They start Off at this lab. Importing the identical file again reports unchanged rows, without duplicates.

tasks.title: Choose the result fields for a test
intro: Do this when people will enter results through this test. Choices come from the installed result dictionary. If none are available, import your system's dictionary first. Terminology explains code lists and Start here explains the CLI. Optional practice includes a fictional dictionary.
steps: Open the test and choose its result fields
Choose Edit from the test row menu. Tick the fields this test produces under its result parameters.
Choose Numeric, Coded or Text for each selected result field. A coded field also needs its configured value set. The example uses Numeric.
For a numeric field needing a reference band, select the dots beside its result-type selector.
Select Add a range. A reference-band form appears below the result field.

tasks.title: Set the reference band and save
intro: Use the bounds approved for your test, method and population. The example band and numbers are fictional and must not be used as clinical ranges.
steps: Enter a name that identifies this reference band. The example uses Example band only.
Enter the lower and upper bounds for your actual test. Blank bounds are open. The screenshot's 1 and 10 are documentation values only.
Set the unit used by this band. Use the same meaning and scale as the actual result.
Set any sex or age limits that apply. An unrestricted band should have no such restriction.
Open the test sheet dots menu and select Save.
tasks.result: The selected fields, result types and reference bands are saved with the test.

tasks.title: Link a received test code to the catalog
intro: Do this after your normal lab data has arrived. If Observed is empty, you can build the catalog now and return later. Enabling a test at this lab and mapping a received code are separate actions.
steps: Select Observed at the top. Tests lists the codes received with orders.
Open the received-code row dots menu and select Map to catalog test.
In Search catalog tests, search for the test this source code actually represents.
Choose the matching catalog test. Check its code as well as its name.
Open the mapping sheet dots menu and select Save.
tasks.result: The received code shows its Catalog test. Reports can count the source code through this catalog identity.

tasks.title: Match received result codes to the dictionary
intro: Result codes identify individual results. They are different from test codes. Exact-code matching is useful when the source and your result dictionary use the same codes. Existing mappings and ambiguous codes are left alone.
steps: Select Results to see received result codes.
Open the Observed dots menu and select Map matching codes.
Choose the source system whose result codes you want to match. If only one exists, it is selected automatically.
Check each code, destination name and result count. Matching names do not replace checking the actual code meanings.
Select the dots in the matching sheet.
Select Map these codes. For different codes, use Map to result field on the received-code row instead.
tasks.result: The matched code names its Result field. If the page reports a stale warehouse copy, its dots menu offers Rebuild warehouse copy.

tasks.title: Link a result field to LOINC
intro: Use a confirmed code for the meaning of your real field. The fictional example only demonstrates the editor. Its illustrative LOINC entry is not a recommendation for your field. A lab receiving the dictionary from central cannot change these links.
steps: Select Result fields. Find the dictionary code and check its role and units.
Open the field row dots menu and select Link LOINC.
Enter or select the confirmed LOINC
When LOINC is loaded, search and select it. Otherwise enter your confirmed code. This installation checks typed code format only. It does not prove the clinical meaning.
Open the LOINC link dots menu and select Save.
tasks.result: The field row shows its LOINC code. Export CSV in the Result fields menu downloads the links.

tasks.title: Use Test catalog on a phone
intro: The same tabs and actions remain available on a phone. Wide tables can scroll horizontally.
steps: Use Tests, Result fields or Observed at the top of the page.
In Tests, the page dots menu is beside the search and table controls. Each row still has its own menu.
In Observed, choose Results when you want received result codes rather than test codes.

end.title: Optional practice with fictional data
paragraphs: Every task above can use your own data. Use these files only in a test installation. A test can be retired, but cannot be deleted. Do not import fictional tests into a live catalog.
html:
• Download a two-test CSV for the import task.
  • Download a one-field result dictionary for the result-field tasks.
  • Download four fictional lab resources to populate Observed.
To follow the pictures exactly, add EXAMPLE-ALPHA manually first. Importing the CSV alone creates Beta and Gamma. Use your own matching names instead if you skip the practice files.
For the optional dictionary and lab-data bundle, first follow Start here. Put the downloaded files in the installation's data folder. From an example development checkout:

cd ~/Downloads/openldr_ce
pnpm openldr terminology import parameters data/example-result-fields.json
pnpm openldr ingest data/example-lab-data.json

For an installed Linux or macOS copy, use ./openldr instead of pnpm openldr. On Windows, use .\openldr.ps1 from your installation folder, such as C:\openldr_ce. Replace the example folder with your real folder. Start here shows the full platform steps.

end.title: Before changing shared catalog data
paragraphs: A catalog received from central has read-only shared definitions. Local availability, local specimen choices and local names remain this lab's settings.
Import accepts at most 5,000 rows and 5 MB. Excel import reads the first worksheet. Tests match by code. A file does not retire tests absent from it or change local settings.
Retiring a test hides it from the default active list. It can be restored. Catalog tests cannot be deleted. Use the Status filter when looking for retired tests.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Add test or Import is missing. Check whether the catalog comes from central and whether your account can manage terminology. Read the ownership message above the table.
A new test is absent from Lab order. Check On at this lab. Creating or importing a test does not automatically enable it.
The import refuses rows. Read each row's reason in Review. Return to Values for unchosen category or specimen text. Check Name and the code or LOINC that supplies its identity.
No result parameters appear. This installation has no usable result fields in its dictionary. Load the dictionary for your system first. The optional practice dictionary is only an example.
A code is still unmapped. Check whether you selected Tests or Results. Mapping one level does not map the other.
The page reports a stale warehouse copy. Open Observed actions and choose Rebuild warehouse copy. The page reports a failure if it cannot rebuild.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Terminology explains configured code lists. Facilities explains facility codes. Start here explains installed and development CLI use.
